raw.core_excitement: The founder is excited by the prospect of a single, intelligent system that can continuously observe work, decide AI actions, and automatically build agents to ensure a "Continuous AI lift" for AI-first companies.
raw.product_description: Narma is an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" with a three-layer architecture. An Intelligence Layer (Layer 2) acts as a "Brain" to detect employee intent, business value of tasks, and "drift" in workflows. An Execution Layer (Layer 3) is an "Agent Factory" that generates, deploys, and monitors AI agents for high-ROI opportunities, with built-in approval gates. It uses existing foundation models and focuses on the "Work Graph" to identify resource burn and mid-flow AI intervention points. The vision is a single system that observes work, decides AI actions, and continuously builds agents for "Continuous AI lift."
raw.thesis: Narma is addressing the critical challenge faced by AI-first enterprises in scaling AI automation. Its core innovation lies in its "Enterprise Agentic Brain" which not only observes and understands how work flows within an organization but also autonomously identifies high-ROI opportunities for AI intervention and then generates and deploys AI agents to execute those tasks. This goes beyond simply providing AI tools; Narma aims to create a continuous, self-optimizing AI system that adapts to and improves enterprise workflows. The target user is AI-first companies that are trying to scale their AI implementations but are struggling with identifying clear ROI, managing drift in AI systems, and accurately measuring the impact of AI. The problem is severe because without such a system, companies invest in AI without clear visibility into its effectiveness, leading to wasted resources and a failure to realize the full potential of AI automation. The founder's goal appears to be a growth startup, aiming to build a scalable solution for a significant and evolving market need. Based on the description, the venture is at the idea stage, with the architecture and vision clearly articulated but no mention of a build or deployed product.
